rows.grounds: fused form: vikāsa (expansion) + āhlāda (delight) + -vat (possessing) + ca (and); describes a universal quality
universal subject continuing from previous verses
nirvṛti (bliss, repose) + yogin (endowed-with, joined-to); compound possessive

items.question: Are expansion, delight, and bliss inherent qualities of all beings?
premises: All beings possess expansion and delight.
All beings are endowed with bliss.
These qualities are attributed universally without exception.
items.inference: Therefore, expansion, delight, and bliss characterize all beings inherently.
uncertainties: nirvṛti may denote bliss, cessation, or final repose depending on doctrinal emphasis.
items.plain_english: And all are possessed of expansion and delight, endowed with bliss.
